title: Lifted surgery: Fast processing with QLDPC codes
authors: Lucas Berent, Lawrence Z. Cohen, Armanda O. Quintavalle
abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes are a leading candidate for achieving low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum computing. However, the time overhead of logical operations in QLDPC codes remains a key challenge. Code surgery, a space-efficient technique for fault-tolerant logical measurements, incurs this overhead through repeated rounds of syndrome measurement. We introduce lifted surgery, a method for fast and parallel surgery on Abelian group algebra codes that maintains the low physical overhead that makes QLDPC codes attractive. Lifted surgery preserves the symmetries of the underlying code, making searches for large instances tractable and offering a natural route towards efficient hardware implementations. We utilise block decompositions and techniques from commutative algebra to characterise lifted surgery, investigate well-behaved subfamilies, and construct explicit examples. In particular, we present quantum radial codes with parameters $[[90, 8, 10]]$ and $[[198, 8, 16 ]]$ for which surgery is fast, parallel, and addressable, allowing arbitrary sets of independent logical operators of the same Pauli type to be measured in a single round of syndrome extraction. We benchmark lifted surgery under circuit-level depolarising noise and, for the $[[ 90, 8, 10 ]]$ code, find logical performance comparable to standard code surgery while requiring ten times fewer rounds of syndrome measurement. By combining speed and parallelism, lifted surgery offers a practical route towards low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum computing.
summary: This paper presents 'lifted surgery,' a novel, algebraically derived technique to drastically reduce the time overhead associated with performing logical measurements on QLDPC quantum error-correcting codes. By leveraging block decompositions and commutative algebra, it achieves fast, parallel syndrome extraction, offering a practical path toward scalable, low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum computing.
main_problem: The primary challenge is overcoming the significant time overhead associated with performing logical operations in Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (QLDPC) codes.
main_result: The authors introduce 'lifted surgery,' a method that achieves fast and parallel code surgery, requiring an order of magnitude fewer syndrome measurement rounds than standard techniques while maintaining low physical overhead.
method: The method utilizes advanced algebraic techniques, including block decompositions and commutative algebra, to characterize and construct the lifted surgery process on Abelian group algebra codes.
model_or_system: The work focuses on QLDPC codes, which are promising candidates for fault-tolerant quantum computation due to their high encoding rates. The analysis is heavily mathematical, involving chain complexes and homology groups.
key_observables: Logical performance, number of syndrome measurement rounds, and the dimension of the measured logical operator space.
important_parameters: Code parameters such as $[[90, 8, 10]]$ and $[[198, 8, 16]]$, and the noise model (circuit-level depolarizing noise).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the algebraic structure of the underlying code algebra, particularly when the blocks are fields, simplifying the addressability criteria.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the graphical representation of lifted surgery, showing the codespace decomposition and the auxiliary complex used to facilitate parallel operations.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the problem (time overhead in code surgery) to introducing the mathematical framework (lifted surgery using algebra), providing explicit constructions (quantum radial codes), and concluding with rigorous mathematical characterizations of addressable submodules and joint measurements.
why_interesting: While focused on QLDPC codes, the underlying mathematical machinery involving homology, chain complexes, and algebraic characterization of measurable operators is highly relevant to theoretical studies of quantum error correction codes in general.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Graphical representation of lifted surgery. (a) Codespace of C• over the group algebra R (blue). (b) The codespace decomposes into the same blocks as the group algebra R. (c) The top row (magenta and orange) shows the auxiliary complex, a copy of C•. Different lifted surgeries can be combined to act in parallel on different blocks. When the blocks are fields, as in the quantum radial code example, lifted surgery allows for single logical qubit addressability.

Figure 2. Graphical representation of bridged lifted surgery. On the bottom row are two copies of the same base codespace, C and C′, over the group algebra R. On the top row is an auxiliary copy of the same codespace, D. The purple sheet connects the auxiliary code D to the two codespaces C and C′

Figure 3. Numerical decoding simulation results. (a) Logical error rates for a single round of lifted (scalar) surgery with the J210, 10, 10K GB and the Gross code. Dashed lines are maximum-likelihood fits and the shaded region corresponds to a 95% confidence region. At p = 10−3 we did not find a logical error for either of the codes in at least 5 × 106 shots. (b) Block error rates per logical operation at p = 10−3 for various numerical surgery experiments on the J90, 8, 10K and J198, 8, 16K radial codes.
